admin.label: Admin panel
admin.summary: A back-office screen: metrics, filtering, sorting and a full create, edit and delete flow.
admin.dataSource: In-memory client state seeded from src/lib/api/account-data.ts
admin.capability: Read and write — every mutation runs through a reducer in the browser

api.label: API demo
api.summary: The same account domain fetched over a real HTTP request, with every response state reachable.
api.dataSource: HTTP GET /api/public/accounts, served by the ASP.NET Core endpoint
api.capability: Read only — paging, search and filtering are computed on the server

page.description: The screen itself: metric band, filter bar, sortable table and the dialogs it opens.

directory.description: The data layer — a reducer plus derived filtering, sorting and metrics. Replaceable by server functions.

presentation.description: Labels, tones, option lists and formatters, so no status or currency is spelled out in a component.

form.description: The create and edit form, sharing one validation function with the data layer.

header.title: Back office, assembled
header.description: A realistic administration screen built only from library components: a metric band, a filterable and sortable data table, a create and edit dialog, row-level actions and a guarded destructive flow — no bespoke styling anywhere.

empty.title: Nothing matches these filters
empty.description: Adjust the search term, segment or status to widen the view.

source.heading: Take this screen with you
source.description: The whole panel is four files: the screen, its data layer, its presentation metadata and the form dialog. They are read from the repository at build time, so copying one gives you exactly what runs here — no snippet drifts out of date.
source.footnote: Records live in a reducer in the browser, which is what makes create, edit and delete instant here. Swap that hook for server functions and no component on this page changes.

deleteDialog.title: Delete {name}?
deleteDialog.description: The account and its balance of {balance} will be removed from the directory. This cannot be undone.

description.edit: Changes are recorded against this account and stamped with the current time.
description.create: The reference is issued automatically once the account is created.

name.label: Account name
name.error: Enter the legal account name (min. 3 characters).

balance.label: Balance
balance.error: Balance must be zero or greater.

validation.name: Enter the legal account name (min. 3 characters).
validation.balanceMinor: Balance must be zero or greater.

header.title: Typed end to end
header.description: One endpoint, one shared contract, four states. Every row below arrives over a real HTTP request against the accounts service, and the same table renders whether the response is populated, slow, empty or a problem document.

states.heading: Response states
states.description: Choose the response returned by the neutral .NET example: populated, slow, empty, or an error in the unified API format.

empty.title: No accounts match this view
empty.emptyScenario: The service answered successfully with zero rows. An empty result is a valid answer, not an error.
empty.noMatch: No account matches the current search and segment. Clear the filters to see the full portfolio.

provenance.heading: Where these rows come from
provenance.description: Nothing on this page is mocked in the component tree. Each row travels the full path below on every request, which is why the latency figure at the top of the page is a real measurement.

referenceData.title: Reference data
referenceData.body: Twelve seeded accounts, held on the server. In the .NET project this is the EF Core seed set.

serverHandler.title: .NET endpoint
serverHandler.body: Applies the segment filter, free-text search and paging, then stamps its own elapsed time on the response.

typedClient.title: Typed client
typedClient.body: Builds the query string, calls the shared API client, and returns typed data without transport mapping.

thisScreen.title: This screen
thisScreen.body: TanStack Query caches per query key; the table renders loading, empty, error and populated from the same tokens.

provenance.comparisonHeading: How this differs from the admin panel

contract.heading: OpenAPI contract
contract.description: The .NET OpenAPI document generates TypeScript types, keeping both sides aligned without handwritten DTO duplication or mapping.

swapCallout.title: Where the real service changes
swapCallout.body: Configure the .NET options and typed HttpClient. React continues to call the same relative /api endpoint through the shared client.

contract.description: OpenAPI generates the TypeScript API shape from the .NET contract; this file is never edited by hand.

client.description: Builds the query string, calls the shared API client, and returns typed data without transport mapping.

handler.description: Neutral .NET endpoint examples and their request/response records.

seed.description: A replaceable typed HTTP client for an optional external service.
